summary: feat(commands): register and index the hand-authored commands written after the print (mva-status, issue #30; recurring-gaps, issue #31)
reason: The generated internal/cli/root.go registers the printed commands one rootCmd.AddCommand at a time, so a command the print never knew has nowhere to be registered without editing it. One line is added there, addHandAuthoredCommands(rootCmd, flags), calling the hand-authored internal/cli/novel_commands.go, which adds every command written after the print; a further command is added in that file and root.go is not touched again. mva-status (internal/cli/mva_status.go) answers which VAT terms are delivered, paid, open or overdue from the structure of the Mva-oppgjør journal entries: a delivery is the settlement entry that touches a VAT account (2700-2719) and belongs to the term its date falls in, a payment is the one that moves 2740 without touching a VAT account and belongs to the term its description names, falling back to the oldest delivered term with a balance. Due dates are one month and ten days after the term ends, 31 August for the third bi-monthly term and 10 March for a yearly term, moved off weekends and Norwegian public holidays. recurring-gaps (internal/cli/recurring_gaps.go) reports, for each (supplier, account) booked in at least --min-months of the --lookback months before a month, the months in the period with no purchase, with the median amount and the last booking; a series whose last booking is more than --ended-after months back is reported as ended, and an unused inbox document naming the supplier in the gap month is noted. Both commands are also listed in the three generated capability indexes, each under a PATCH(term-commands) marker: whichIndex in internal/cli/which.go, the Highlights block of the root command's Long text in internal/cli/root.go, and command_mirror_capabilities in internal/mcp/tools.go; .printing-press.json novel_features carries the same two entries. The mva-summary and missing-bilag blurbs in those indexes were brought in line with issues #24 and #28 in the same edit.
